title: Strap a carton to a luggage cart with a bungee: hook each end round a frame tube, the second against the cord's pull
instruction: Strap the carton onto the luggage cart with the bungee cord: hook one end on each side tube of the cart's frame, with the cord stretched round the front of the carton at about half its height, then let go of the cord.
context: People strap a box or bag onto a folding luggage cart with its bungee cord whenever they wheel luggage, a parcel or shopping somewhere. Not stated: a J-hook goes onto an upright tube from behind: it is reached past the tube, slid in behind it and drawn forward into its bend. Once the first hook is on, the second must be placed this way while the stretched cord pulls it back with 8 to 12 N and the arm gives under that pull; let go before the tube is inside its bend, it flies back across the carton and pulls the first hook off with it. Strapped round the middle of the carton, the load stays on the nose plate when the cart is tilted back, rocked and tipped forward; unstrapped it slides off. Unlike ratcheting a webbing tie-down tight with lever strokes and latching its handle, or moving a boxed load with a hand truck, the skill here is setting a hook precisely round a tube against an elastic pull.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left), heights above the table. Folding steel luggage cart (about 2.6 kg), standing upright facing the arms and held still by a clamp over its axle (standing in for a foot on the axle): steel nose plate 38 cm wide x 26 cm deep x 0.4 cm, flat on the table, spanning x 19.6 to 45.6, centred on y 0; two upright side tubes, steel, 16 mm across, at x 44.8, y 17 and y -17, from the plate to 60 cm up, continuing as a telescoping handle (13 mm tubes) to 100 cm with a black foam grip across the top; three 16 mm cross tubes between the side tubes at 3, 10 and 40 cm above the plate; two black rubber wheels 10 cm across, 2.5 cm wide, on an axle at x 48.5, 5 cm up, wheels at y 23.5 and -23.5. Carton: single-wall corrugated board, brown, 22 cm deep x 24 cm wide x 24 cm tall, 1.2 kg (with contents), tape across the top, standing on the nose plate centred at x 32.8, y 0, its back against the cross tubes. Bungee cord: 24 in (61 cm over the hooks), 6 mm yellow elastic, 50 cm between its two crimp sleeves when relaxed, 112 N per metre of stretch (estimate); at each end a red plastic-coated steel J-hook of 6 mm wire, 20 mm clear opening, rounded bend, 7 cm long with a 2.6 cm steel crimp sleeve (30 g with its share of the cord). The cord lies on the table in front of the cart, the hooks flat with their shanks pointing toward the arms, at x 30, y 23.5 and y -23.5 (crimp sleeves 49.6 cm apart, the cord just slack). Strapped as asked, the cord is about 57 cm long and pulls with about 8 N.
scoring: Judged from the video and, at the end, a ruler, a phone level and a tape mark on the nose plate round the carton. A hook is home on a side tube when the tube passes through its bend (between the bend and the end of the tip) and the hook lies within 35 degrees of flat. The cord is round the carton when it bends round both of the carton's front vertical edges; it must cross each of them 6 to 18 cm above the nose plate. The carton stands on the nose plate when the middle of its bottom is on the plate, within 2 cm of it, and the carton leans less than 20 degrees from the frame's upright. 0.25: at least one hook home, the carton standing on the nose plate and the cord stretched round the carton's front (held or not). 0.5: both hooks home, one on each side tube, the cord round the front within that band, the carton on the plate, both grippers at least 3 cm from the hooks and the carton and 2 cm from the cord, and neither hook nor the carton moving more than 3 mm in 0.5 s. When all of this has held for 1 s, the test starts (in simulation the scorer moves the cart; by hand, take off the axle clamp and use the handle): tilt the cart back 45 degrees on its wheels, rock it 20 degrees to each side about the frame's long axis, stand it up, lift it 15 cm, tip it 30 degrees forward about the axle and back upright (20 s). 1.0: through the whole test the carton stays on the nose plate and moves less than 4 cm on it, both hooks are still home at the end, and the grippers stay as clear of the hooks, carton and cord as for 0.5; otherwise the trial stays at 0.5. Anything else scores 0.
reset_notes: Take the cord off, lay it straight on the table in front of the cart with both hooks pointing toward the arms at the marked spots, and stand the carton back on its mark against the frame.
fidelity: The cart is rigid and held still by a clamp over its axle while the robot works. For the test the scorer moves it by setting its pose (by hand: back 45 degrees, rock 20 degrees each way, lift 15 cm, tip forward 30 degrees), ending with it held up. The cord is a massless elastic line (112 N/m, an estimate) that wraps the carton's front edges without friction, does not touch the robot and is drawn as segments. Carton-on-steel friction 0.35 and the cart's 2.6 kg are estimates; the carton is rigid.
